days.title: Walk for 15 minutes
days.description: Lace up any comfortable shoes and head out for a brisk 15-minute walk. Focus on your breathing and how your body feels.
days.tip: Maintain a pace where you can still hold a conversation comfortably

days.title: Introduce short run intervals
days.description: Walk for 5 minutes to warm up. Then, alternate 30 seconds of slow jogging with 2 minutes of walking, repeating 5 times. Cool down with a 5-minute walk.
days.tip: Keep your running pace easy – it should feel like you could go on longer

days.title: Focus on running form
days.description: Watch a beginner video on running form (e.g., posture, foot strike). Then, do a 20-minute walk with short 1-minute run intervals, consciously applying one form tip.
days.tip: Aim for light, quick steps rather than long strides to reduce impact

days.title: Increase run duration slightly
days.description: Warm up with a 5-minute walk. Then, alternate 1 minute of jogging with 2 minutes of walking, repeating 6 times. Cool down with a 5-minute walk.
days.tip: Listen to your body; it's okay to shorten run intervals if you feel too tired

days.title: Rest and active recovery
days.description: Engage in light stretching or a gentle 15-minute walk. Allow your muscles to recover after your previous runs.
days.tip: Recovery is as important as running for preventing injury and building strength

days.title: Extend your total run time
days.description: Warm up with a 5-minute walk. Then, alternate 90 seconds of jogging with 2 minutes of walking, repeating 5 times. Finish with a 5-minute cool-down walk.
days.tip: Gradually increasing your run time prevents burnout and overuse injuries

days.title: Week 1 review and plan
days.description: Reflect on how your body felt this week. Note what was easy, what was challenging, and what you'd like to achieve next week. Plan your runs for the coming days.
days.tip: Consistency, not speed, is the most crucial factor for beginner runners
